materials.name: Plastic Kinematic
materials.summary: Elastic–plastic with linear hardening (ETAN). Isotropic/kinematic/combined via BETA. Common for rebar and structural steel.

inputs.label: Material ID (MID)
inputs.hint: Unique positive integer material ID (e.g., 1, 12, 1001).

inputs.label: Density RO
inputs.hint: Steel typical: 0.00785 g/mm^3 (≈7850 kg/m^3). Use your test/spec value if known.

inputs.label: Young's modulus E
inputs.hint: Typical steels: 200000–210000 MPa. Use coupon/test value when possible.

inputs.label: Poisson ratio PR
inputs.hint: Metals typically 0.25–0.33. Keep <0.5 for stability.

inputs.label: Yield stress SIGY (fy)
inputs.hint: Yield / 0.2% proof stress from tensile test.

inputs.label: Tangent modulus ETAN
inputs.hint: Post-yield linear hardening slope. Typical steel: ETAN ≈ 0.2%–2% of E. Prefer calibration to test stress–strain or cyclic hysteresis.

inputs.label: Hardening mix BETA
inputs.hint: 0 = kinematic, 1 = isotropic, 0–1 = combined (LS-DYNA manual, MAT_003 Remark 2). For cyclic steel, calibrate to the Bauschinger effect / hysteresis.

inputs.label: SRC (optional)
inputs.hint: Cowper–Symonds C in 1/ms for this unit system (C in 1/s ÷ 1000; mild steel 40.4 1/s → 0.0404). Blank = no rate effect.

inputs.label: SRP (optional)
inputs.hint: Cowper–Symonds P (rate effect). A common starting point for mild steel is P≈5, with C calibrated (problem dependent).

inputs.label: FS (optional)
inputs.hint: Effective plastic strain at which elements erode. Leave blank for no erosion (LS-DYNA default 1E20).

inputs.label: VP
inputs.hint: 0 = scale yield stress (default), 1 = viscoplastic formulation (recommended by the manual).

inputs.label: Material ID (MID)
inputs.hint: Example MID = 15.

inputs.label: Density
inputs.hint: Steel ~0.00785 g/mm³.

inputs.label: Young's modulus
inputs.hint: Typical steel ~210000 MPa.

inputs.label: Poisson ratio
inputs.hint: Typical steel ~0.30.

inputs.label: A (yield stress)
inputs.hint: Example value only.

inputs.label: B (hardening)
inputs.hint: Example value only.

inputs.label: n (hardening exponent)
inputs.hint: Common range: 0.1–0.7.

inputs.label: C (rate effect)
inputs.hint: Set small if rate effects are not used.

inputs.label: m (thermal softening)
inputs.hint: Used with temperature-dependent terms.

inputs.label: Melt temperature
inputs.hint: TM on card 2. Steel ~1793 K (varies by alloy).

inputs.label: Reference strain rate
inputs.hint: Quasi-static threshold rate. Entered in 1/s; written to the card in 1/ms (x 1e-3).

inputs.label: Specific heat CP
inputs.hint: Steel ~450–480. Same number in mJ/(g·K) for this unit system.

inputs.label: Tensile cutoff PC
inputs.hint: Must be ≤ 0. -1E20 disables spall; with SPALL=2 a value of 0 would remove all tensile stress.

inputs.label: Rate formulation VP
inputs.hint: 0 = scale yield stress (default), 1 = viscoplastic.

inputs.label: Damage D1 (optional)
inputs.hint: Leave D1–D5 blank to switch off JC failure (EROD=1).

materials.name: Piecewise Linear Plasticity
materials.summary: MAT_024 employs the Yun & Gardner (2017) engineering stress–strain envelope to define a rational steel material curve in the absence of experimental data, implemented as a true stress–true plastic strain curve via DEFINE_CURVE. Optional ductile fracture from the reduction of area Z, as FAIL or *MAT_ADD_DAMAGE_GISSMO, calibrated on BAM S355 tensile tests.

inputs.label: Material ID (MID)
inputs.hint: Unique positive integer material ID.

inputs.label: Density RO
inputs.hint: Steel typical: 0.00785 g/mm^3.

inputs.label: Young's modulus E
inputs.hint: Typical steels: 200000–210000 MPa.

inputs.label: Poisson ratio PR
inputs.hint: Metals typically 0.25–0.33.

inputs.label: Yield stress Fy
inputs.hint: Yield / 0.2% proof stress from tensile test.

inputs.label: Ultimate stress Fu
inputs.hint: Ultimate tensile strength (engineering).

inputs.label: Points: yield plateau
inputs.hint: Discretization only: number of points on yield plateau (σ = Fy). More points = smoother curve, not different material.

inputs.label: Points: hardening
inputs.hint: Discretization only: number of points for nonlinear hardening (Fy → Fu). More points = smoother curve.

inputs.label: Extension beyond A_g, Δεp
inputs.hint: Length of the straight extension of the curve beyond A_g, in true plastic strain. Keep it above FAIL.

inputs.label: Slope beyond A_g, H / σ(A_g)
inputs.hint: Slope of the extension as a multiple of the true stress at A_g. 1 = Considère slope, the neck starts at A_g (calibrated value). 0 = flat tail (versions ≤ 1.1).

inputs.label: Reduction of area Z (optional)
inputs.hint: Measured reduction of area at fracture. Blank = no fracture (FAIL = 0).

inputs.label: Element size in the neck
inputs.hint: Used only with Z and fracture model 0: FAIL = k(h) · ln(1/(1−Z)), with k calibrated for 8-node solids. GISSMO regularises every element size itself.

inputs.label: Fracture model
inputs.hint: Used only with Z. 0 = FAIL (element erosion, abrupt), 1 = *MAT_ADD_DAMAGE_GISSMO (gradual load drop, any element size).

materials.name: K&C Damage Release 3
materials.summary: K&C Damage Release III concrete model with DIF curve + tabulated compaction EOS.

inputs.hint: Measured mean cylinder strength of the concrete you model (= f_cm, e.g. 38 for C30/37).

inputs.label: Element size h
inputs.hint: Edge length of the elements where cracks form. The damage function is scaled so that one cracked element dissipates G_F.

inputs.label: Fracture energy G_F (optional)
inputs.hint: Blank = fib MC2010: 73 f_cm^0.18 N/m (0.135 N/mm at 30 MPa).

inputs.label: Omega (ω)

inputs.label: Strain-rate DIF model
inputs.hint: 0 = off (LCRATE = 0; use for quasi-static runs), 1 = CEB-FIP MC90 compression + Malvar & Ross tension, 2 = fib Model Code 2010.

inputs.label: DIF rate cap
inputs.hint: DIF held constant above this strain rate (the manual's sample curve stops rising at 300 1/s).
